panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Wide museum-floor establishing panel: school visitors clustered around brighter exhibits, a tired attendant at a desk, civic display cases and scuffed public flooring. Theo has stopped alone at one small plain case in the foreground while Rae and Adrian are several steps farther down the gallery.

Panel 2 — Close on the worn attaché satchel behind glass. Theo says, 'That's mine.' Nothing glows or activates; recognition comes from scratches, softened corners and a clasp that sits slightly wrong.
Panel 3 — Rae asks, 'You're sure?' Theo answers, 'The clasp sticks on the left.' Show his hand unconsciously making the old opening motion before he catches himself.
Panel 4 — Adrian says only, 'Theo.' Theo turns toward the museum label and asks how old the sign says it is. Adrian's discomfort is interpersonal, not technical.
Panel 5 — Adrian: 'Don't read the sign.' End with Theo already reading it while his remembered ownership and the institution's confident false interpretation occupy the same quiet frame.

Panel 1 — Ancient Tyrellis waystation kitchen late in the day. A cup has gone cold beside Flux. Afterlight finds them still sitting where others left them hours ago. Keep the room small, practical and tired.

Panel 2 — Afterlight stands in the kitchen doorway with one shoulder against the frame. Flux remains seated at the table beside the cold cup, coat still on, gaze fixed on the closed council-room door. 'They're waiting for you.' / 'They've been waiting for me since breakfast.'
Panel 3 — Afterlight notes that it is nearly dark. Flux answers, 'Then they're improving.' Give the joke a thin edge; exhaustion is visible underneath it.
Panel 4 — Afterlight: 'Mero needs an answer.' Flux looks toward the closed door where the decision-makers are waiting, but does not rise.
Panel 5 — Flux: 'Mero needs permission. That's different.' Afterlight looks from Flux to the closed council-room door, then pulls out the chair opposite him and sits instead of urging him toward it.
Panel 1 — Rae and Theo in the municipal archive beneath the museum. Paper, reused bindings and ordinary clerical wear dominate; avoid futuristic data-display spectacle.
Panel 2 — Rae pauses over a later civic volume and says, 'This is mine.' Theo assumes she means the handwriting.
Panel 3 — Insert on one tiny correction in the margin, physically incorporated into a later binding. Rae: 'The correction.' The evidence is mundane enough to be harder to dismiss.

Panel 4 — Theo: 'That's worse somehow.' Rae lays two reused records side by side and traces matching physical repairs, handwriting and ownership marks across them; no hidden screen or archive mechanism appears.

Panel 5 — Rae: 'Because nobody preserved it. They just kept using it.' End tight on layers of old paper: erased headings, later annotations, patched tears and fresh present-day handling marks occupying the same sheets.
Panel 1 — Ancient council room after the argument has emptied out. Chairs stand crooked around abandoned papers; Mero remains at the table and Flux is the only other person still in the room.

Panel 2 — Medium two-shot across the abandoned council table. Mero leans forward with both palms on scattered papers: 'Tell me which choice survives.' Flux looks from the papers to Mero's face, then folds one sheet closed before answering.
Panel 3 — Flux: 'You mean which choice lets you sleep.' Mero: 'I haven't slept in months.' Keep both exhausted, not theatrical.

Panel 4 — Flux: 'Then stop asking me to dream for you.' Mero grips the back of an empty chair until his knuckles whiten, then releases it and steps away from the table instead of answering immediately.

Panel 5 — Mero: 'I need something.' Flux: 'You need to choose without pretending the future chose for you.' Flux pushes the folded paper back across the table and leaves Mero standing alone among the empty chairs.

directionInline.text: Use the stairwell itself as visual evidence: lower courses are ancient dark stone, upper repairs are paler modern masonry, and worn stair edges continue across the transition. Keep Theo and Adrian in medium full-body frames moving downward; no screens or diagrams appear.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo and Adrian descend an ordinary stairwell where ancient stone continues into modern repairs with no clean boundary. Theo asks, 'How much time is missing?'
Panel 2 — Adrian: 'That's not what was removed.' He keeps descending the stairs while Theo and Rae stop above him. Adrian does not turn toward the museum labels or offer any visual aid.

Panel 3 — Theo stops on the stairs and points upward toward the museum level: 'Then why does everything call us ancient?' Keep the old lower stone courses and newer upper masonry visible in the same vertical frame.
Panel 4 — Adrian: 'Because the world needed a story that connected yesterday to today.' Theo: 'And it made one up?'

Panel 5 — Adrian stops on a landing where dark ancient stone continues directly into pale modern repair with matching worn stair edges: 'It healed around the wound.' Theo stands one step below him, looking at the continuous masonry instead of Adrian.
Panel 1 — Ancient balcony at dusk above refugee movement. Flux and Starbreaker stand apart from the traffic below; keep the human evacuation legible so their argument has people attached to it.
Panel 2 — Starbreaker: 'You've seen what happens if I wait.' Flux: 'I've seen what happens if you don't.' Neither future is visualized as a clean prophetic diagram.

Panel 3 — Starbreaker closes the distance until he and Flux are nearly face-to-face: 'So pick one.' Flux stays against the balcony rail, hands open and empty: 'That's your job.' Refugees continue moving below them.
Panel 4 — Starbreaker: 'Coward.' Let Flux absorb it; for a beat they are unsure whether he is wrong.
Panel 5 — Flux: 'Maybe. But I won't turn fear into permission for you.' End with Starbreaker looking back toward the people whose fate he still has to choose about.

Panel 1 — Theo and Rae emerge into an ordinary evening market built over ancient foundations. Vendors close stalls, families move through, someone argues over a purchase. The present is visibly a real life, not scenery waiting to be corrected.
Panel 2 — Theo: 'They're living on a lie.' Rae: 'They're living.' Keep the surrounding people unaware of the protagonists' philosophical crisis.

Panel 3 — Theo: 'That's your answer?' Rae: 'It's the part you keep skipping.' Rae points through the public window toward families crossing the plaza below; Theo follows her finger instead of looking back at the monument.
Panel 4 — Theo asks, 'And if they were there too?' The question changes the passersby from background to possible owners of lost histories.
Panel 5 — Rae: 'Then we still don't get to decide for them.' End on Theo watching one ordinary family pass, forced to consider that truth does not automatically grant authority.
Panel 1 — Return to the ancient kitchen late at night. Flux packs one small bag on the chair. The same cold cup from the morning remains untouched on the table beside a dried ring of spilled drink.
Panel 2 — Afterlight: 'You're leaving.' Flux: 'I'm trying.' Afterlight steps sideways out of the doorway and leaves a clear path to the hall; her hands stay at her sides.
Panel 3 — Afterlight: 'Where?' Flux stops with one hand on the doorframe and the packed bag hanging from the other. He stares into the empty corridor before answering.

Panel 4 — Flux stands with the small packed bag in hand at the open doorway: 'Somewhere nobody asks me what happens next.' Afterlight remains beside the table and cold cup: 'That place doesn't exist.' Neither moves toward the other.
Panel 5 — Flux: 'Then maybe I'll finally be surprised.' End on the cold cup and the open doorway after Flux moves toward it; do not imply where they go or foreshadow a technical explanation.

directionInline.text: Stage Theo, Rae and Adrian at an ordinary archive table surrounded by reused books, repaired walls and mismatched records. Adrian sits for the first time; Rae and Theo face him from opposite sides. Keep explanations grounded in faces, hands and physical records on the table.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Archive after closing. Adrian finally sits at an ordinary table with Rae and Theo instead of pacing away from the question.

Panel 2 — Rae: 'Which parts are real?' Adrian answers, 'All of them.' Keep all three at the physical table with books and records between them; Rae presses one palm onto the open pages while Adrian meets her eyes.
Panel 3 — Theo: 'That's useless.' Adrian: 'It's also true.' The argument stays between people.
Panel 4 — Rae: 'You don't know where the seam is.' Adrian looks at reused records, repaired walls and the two present people in front of him.

Panel 5 — Adrian: 'I don't think there is one seam.' End in a wide table shot: Rae has two reused volumes open, Theo holds a repaired document, and behind Adrian an old wall patch disappears into newer masonry with no clean dividing line.
Panel 1 — Ancient kitchen the next morning. The same cup is still where Flux left it. Their chair is empty. Nothing is damaged and nothing announces an event.
Panel 2 — Mero enters looking for Flux and immediately knows something is wrong from Afterlight's face, not from an alarm.
Panel 3 — Mero: 'When did you last see them?' Afterlight: 'Last night.' Keep the empty place visible between them.
Panel 4 — Mero asks whether Flux said where and whether Afterlight asked. Her answers are simply 'No' and 'Yes.'
Panel 5 — End on the untouched cup, empty chair and ordinary doorway. No portal, residue, body, message or Reset effect. This absence is genuinely unexplained.

Panel 1 — Present transit platform among ordinary commuters. Theo grips a rail and briefly assumes the same shoulder angle as his ancient staff posture; Rae's hand pauses over a ticket as her gaze fixes on a passing stranger. No visual effect surrounds either of them.
Panel 2 — Theo: 'I told him something.' Rae: 'Mero?' He remembers the emotional fact before the full scene.
Panel 3 — Theo: 'I told him everyone was getting addicted to certainty.' He is unsettled that the thought sounds like him now.
Panel 4 — Rae: 'I argued with Arbiter.' Theo asks whether it was about the decision.

Panel 5 — Rae: 'About what we called the people inside it.' End on an old record open between Theo and Rae, with their own ancient handwriting or classifications visible beside names of ordinary people; both stare down at the marks they once made.

Panel 1 — Same ordinary transit platform. A worker pauses mid-announcement and says, 'No. That's not what it was called.' Nearby commuters stop walking and look toward the worker while the departure flow continues behind them.
Panel 2 — Rae approaches gently: 'What did you call it?' The worker cannot answer despite the certainty that interrupted them.
Panel 3 — Rae: 'You just said you did.' The worker's confusion turns to grief before any historical context arrives.
Panel 4 — Worker: 'My brother died there.' Theo asks, carefully, 'Do you have a brother?'
Panel 5 — Worker: 'No.' Hold on the contradiction: present biography and recovered grief are both emotionally real.

Panel 6 — Final reaction on Adrian at the edge of the platform, face suddenly still as he watches the grieving worker. Behind him commuters continue boarding, a departure board changes normally and the station staff keep working.
